features.name: dmClock admission gate for client metadata requests
features.description: Every CEPH_MSG_CLIENT_REQUEST is routed from Server::dispatch to MDSDmclockScheduler::handle_client_request. Requests are queued only when QoS is enabled, the original source is a client, the rank is up:active, the session's volume entry exists and has been updated, and its effective reservation, weight and limit are all > 0. Otherwise the request goes straight to Server::handle_client_request.
features.notes: Disabled by default. Only MClientRequest is gated: caps, cap releases, leases, session messages, peer requests, MDS-originated client requests and internal ops are not.

features.name: Session-to-volume classification by mount root
features.description: Volume id = session client_metadata['root'] truncated to its first 3 path components (SUBVOL_ROOT_DEPTH=3). Paths of depth <= 3 are used verbatim. A missing root gives the '' bucket. Per-request classification always uses the session, never the request path.
code_refs: src/mds/CInode.cc:5597 (CInode::get_subvolume_id, authoritative inode-to-subvolume mapping not used by QoS)
features.notes: The root is client-asserted (kclient server_path, libcephfs mount_root, overridable via client_metadata), checked against MDSAuthCaps::path_capable at session open. Root-mounted clients (mgr, Ganesha default cmount_path=/) share the '/' bucket. mgr volumes (mgr_util.py:251) and cephfs-mirror (Utils.cc:138) mount with an empty root, which becomes '/'. The MDS already has an authoritative inode-to-subvolume mapping (CInode::get_subvolume_id via the subvolume snaprealm, used for subvolume metrics); the QoS gate does not use it.

features.name: Per-op cost table
features.description: Cost 1 for LOOKUP, LOOKUPHASH, LOOKUPPARENT, LOOKUPINO, LOOKUPNAME, GETATTR, READDIR, OPEN, LOOKUPSNAP, LSSNAP and GETFILELOCK. Cost 3 for every other op: the explicit mutation list plus the default arm, which covers the read-only GETVXATTR, READDIR_SNAPDIFF and FILE_BLOCKDIFF, the mutating SNAP_METADATA and the unused DUMMY.
features.notes: Documented in doc/cephfs/mds-qos.rst as read-like=1 and mutating=3. Fixed at enqueue time; independent of request size and outcome.

features.name: dmClock push queue with reservation, weight and limit tags
features.description: crimson::dmclock::PushPriorityQueue<VolumeId, ClientRequest>: immediate tag calculation, cached ClientInfo (U1=false), AtLimit::Wait, ReqParams{0,0}, can_handle always true, idle 300 s, erase 600 s, clean every 60 s. Reservation phase first, then ready-by-proportion phase. No limit break.
features.notes: Analysis: with no capacity model it acts mainly as a per-volume, per-rank limit of about max(reservation, limit) cost units/s. Weight and reservation only order requests that are eligible together.

features.name: Scheduler thread and synchronous hand-off to the MDS
features.description: A dedicated scheduler thread drains the FIFO request_queue into dmClock. The eligible request is handed off on the scheduler thread or the dmClock sched-ahead thread by submit_request_to_mds, which takes mds_lock and calls Server::handle_client_request while dmClock data_mtx is held.
features.notes: 3 threads per MDSRank, always started. The sched-ahead thread's wait_until returns immediately (predicate already true), so it re-polls rather than sleeps (code reading).

features.name: Cluster-wide default QoS via config options
features.description: mds_dmclock_enable (bool, default false), mds_dmclock_reservation, mds_dmclock_weight and mds_dmclock_limit (float, default 1000.0, runtime). The MDS tracks all four; changes are applied on the MDSRank finisher under mds_lock.
features.notes: Defaults apply to every volume without an override, including '/' and ''. Values <= 0 (or NaN) make the gate bypass default-using volumes for new requests, but requests already in the FIFO are tagged with the new value through the default_conf pointer (a 0 gives +inf tags and can stall the volume). Setting NaN trips ceph_assert(stored == config) in handle_conf_change when that key changes, even with QoS disabled, and on any tracked-option change while QoS is enabled.

features.name: Per-volume override admin commands
features.description: qos set <path> <reservation> <weight> <limit> (integers >= 1, reservation <= limit, volume must already exist) and qos rm <path>. Both enqueue an UpdateRequest that the scheduler thread applies asynchronously.
features.notes: Memory only and per rank. Lost on restart or failover and when the volume's last session on that rank closes. Command r is always 0; failure appears as return_code 0 plus a status string.

features.name: QoS inspection commands
features.description: dump qos (global state plus all volumes) and qos get <path> (one volume): use_default, triple, throttle (DecayCounter, 60 s half-life), latency_avg (queueing delay), inflight_requests (queued in dmClock), session_cnt and session_list.
features.notes: Not exposed as perf counters, health or mgr metrics. Not shown by ceph fs status. mds_dmclock_queue_size is the FIFO size, not the dmClock queue size.

features.name: Volume-info lifecycle tied to sessions
features.description: VolumeInfo is created on the first add_session for a root while enabled (from journaled open, reconnect, force-open/import, or enable), and erased when its session set becomes empty (journaled close or kill).
features.notes: Erase asserts inflight==0, so evicting the last session of a throttled volume can crash the MDS (code reading). inflight does not count FIFO entries: a request still in the FIFO when its volume is erased hits the increase_inflight_request assert, or, if the volume was re-created meanwhile, is tagged through a stale dmClock record whose info pointer can dangle (override) or be null. remove_session is a no-op while disabled, so stale session ids accumulate.

features.name: Enable and drain on rank state and option changes
features.description: active_start enables QoS if the option is set and adds all OPEN/STALE sessions. stopping_start and switching the option off disable it: drop mds_lock, wait for the FIFO to drain (1 s sleeps), then cancel_inflight_request flushes the dmClock queue directly to the MDS. active_start and stopping_start run on the messenger dispatch thread inside MDSRankDispatcher::handle_mds_map; option changes run on the mds-rank-fin finisher.
code_refs: src/mds/MDSRank.cc:564 (~MDSRank deletes the scheduler after server and mdcache)
features.notes: cancel_inflight_request re-locks the non-recursive volume_info_lock through submit_request_to_mds->hit_volume_throttle (self-deadlock when the queue is non-empty), and inverts the volume_info_lock/data_mtx order (code reading). When reached from stopping_start, the sleeps and any deadlock stall all message dispatch, and mds_lock is released in the middle of handle_mds_map. The scheduler is only torn down in ~MDSRank, after server and mdcache are deleted, so a drain at clean shutdown would call into a deleted Server.

features.name: Per-volume throttle and latency statistics
features.description: At hand-off: latency = now - arrival (FIFO plus dmClock wait, CLOCK_REALTIME). latency_avg halves sum and count at 1000 samples. throttle is incremented when latency > 1/limit and inflight > limit.
features.notes: Excludes mds_lock wait and MDS processing time.

features.name: Op tracking interaction
features.description: Queued requests have no MDRequest and are invisible to ops dumps and counters. Once dispatched, op age starts at the message receive stamp, so queue time counts toward slow-request complaints. l_mds_request and l_mdss_handle_client_request count at hand-off.
features.notes: MDS_SLOW_REQUEST health can be triggered by QoS delay.

features.name: Unbounded queues without back-pressure
features.description: The FIFO request_queue and the dmClock per-volume deques have no size bound. The messenger dispatch throttle is released when ms_dispatch returns, before QoS queueing. AtLimit::Wait never rejects.
features.notes: Clients see only latency. The kclient mount-time root GETATTR times out after mount_timeout (60 s); libcephfs aborts mount requests after client_mount_timeout (300 s).

features.name: Unimplemented vxattr-based QoS hook
features.description: MDSDmclockScheduler::read_xattrs(VolumeId) is declared but has no definition or caller. There is no ceph.* vxattr or subvolume metadata for QoS, and the mgr volumes module has no QoS commands.
features.notes: Gateway QoS for NFS (nfs cluster/export qos) and SMB lives in the gateways, not in the MDS.

features.name: Gate bypass for non-active ranks and MDS-originated requests
features.description: Requests reaching the gate in up:clientreplay (replayed or queued-for-replay) or up:stopping bypass QoS. New requests that arrive while the rank is not active are parked with wait_for_active and pass the gate (and can be throttled) once up:active. MClientRequests sent MDS to MDS (stray reintegration and migration renames) bypass because their source is not a client. Client metrics messages use a separate dispatcher.
features.notes: Only the initial dispatch of a client message is gated; C_MDS_RetryMessage retries re-enter the gate, C_MDS_RetryRequest retries do not.

serialization_points.name: QoS hand-off takes mds_lock while holding dmClock data_mtx
serialization_points.shared_state: Entire MDS (mds_lock) plus every volume's dmClock state (data_mtx)
serialization_points.why_serialized: Server::handle_client_request needs mds_lock. dmClock calls handle_f from inside pop_process_request with data_mtx held, so only one hand-off across all volumes can be in progress.
serialization_points.notes: Real conflicts are only among requests touching the same inodes and dentries. The admission decision itself is per volume.

serialization_points.name: Single dmClock queue mutex for all volumes
serialization_points.shared_state: client_map and the reservation, limit and ready heaps for every volume
serialization_points.why_serialized: One PushPriorityQueue instance serves all volumes. add_request, scheduling, cleaning and update_client_info all take data_mtx.
serialization_points.notes: Limit and reservation tags are per volume. Only proportional (weight) ordering across volumes needs shared state.

serialization_points.name: Single scheduler thread with one FIFO
serialization_points.shared_state: request_queue (all gated requests of all volumes, plus UpdateRequests)
serialization_points.why_serialized: A single consumer thread moves requests into dmClock and synchronously dispatches. When mds_lock is busy, the whole backlog waits in this unordered FIFO.

serialization_points.name: Global volume_info_lock
serialization_points.why_serialized: One std::mutex guards the map and all per-volume counters and statistics.
serialization_points.notes: Per-volume state could be locked per volume. The map structure changes only on session add/remove.

serialization_points.name: Gate classification under mds_lock on the dispatch thread
serialization_points.shared_state: Session metadata, VolumeInfo lookups, FIFO append
serialization_points.why_serialized: All client messages are dispatched under mds_lock on the single ms_dispatch thread.
serialization_points.notes: Classification reads immutable session metadata only.

serialization_points.name: Per-volume FIFO shared by all sessions of the volume
serialization_points.shared_state: Arrival order of all sessions in one volume
serialization_points.why_serialized: dmClock treats the volume as one client with one deque. Only the head competes.
serialization_points.notes: Clients only need per-session ordering. A slow head blocks other sessions of the same subvolume.

serialization_points.name: Single sched-ahead dispatcher
serialization_points.why_serialized: One thread re-polls schedule_request() under data_mtx for all future-eligible requests.

serialization_points.name: Disable/drain loops with 1 s sleeps
serialization_points.shared_state: The mds-rank-fin finisher (option change) or the messenger dispatch thread (stopping_start inside MDSRankDispatcher::handle_mds_map), plus the QoS queues
serialization_points.why_serialized: Draining is done by polling with sleeps on the caller's thread, dropping mds_lock in between.
serialization_points.notes: Blocks the finisher, or all message dispatch to the daemon, for >= 2 s; indefinitely if cancel_inflight_request deadlocks.

serialization_points.name: QoS admin commands under mds_lock
serialization_points.why_serialized: The asok handler takes mds_lock for dump qos and qos set/rm/get, although the scheduler uses its own locks.
serialization_points.notes: The commands only touch QoS-private state.

external_contract.item: Session metadata 'root' determines the QoS bucket
external_contract.detail: The kclient sends root = canonicalized server_path (leading '/', no duplicate or trailing slashes), or '/' when there is none, in CEPH_SESSION_REQUEST_OPEN metadata. The MDS uses its first 3 components as the volume id.
No error, no EAGAIN, no new message. Ordinary requests wait without timeout. The mount-time root GETATTR uses mount_timeout (60 s) and can fail with -ETIMEDOUT under a long backlog.

metadata['root'] = mount_root ('/' default). The client_metadata option can override root. Sessions opened by start_reclaim before mount carry no root and are reused by the mount (code reading), so a reclaiming client lands in the '' bucket.
During mount, Client::tick aborts the first MDS request with -ETIMEDOUT after client_mount_timeout (300 s). QoS delay counts toward it.
The nfs mgr module defaults cmount_path to '/'. Exports sharing that cephfs mount share one '/' bucket (the Ganesha-side mapping is unverified).

external_contract.item: Message ordering relative to caps, leases and session messages
external_contract.detail: Gated requests can be overtaken by later non-request messages (caps, cap releases, leases, session messages) on the same connection, which are handled immediately. Without QoS, a connection's messages are handled in arrival order by the single dispatch thread (no fast dispatch in the MDS). Per-session request order holds only among queued requests.

external_contract.item: Admin commands dump qos / qos set / qos rm / qos get
external_contract.detail: Via ceph tell mds.<id> (needs allow * caps) or the asok. qos set takes path plus CephInt reservation, weight and limit (>= 1, reservation <= limit). Outputs: results.return_code 1/0, volume_qos_info, qos_info.qos_state and volume_infos. Command r is always 0.

external_contract.item: Config options in the config DB
external_contract.detail: mds_dmclock_enable=false, mds_dmclock_reservation=1000.0, mds_dmclock_weight=1000.0, mds_dmclock_limit=1000.0 (runtime). Set with ceph config set mds ...
No mgr module (volumes, nfs, cephadm, dashboard, stats) uses the qos commands or mds_dmclock_* options. ceph fs status shows nothing. MDS QoS state is not in MDSMap/FSMap.
external_contract.code_ref: grep of src/pybind for dmclock / qos set / dump qos

external_contract.detail: QoS state is never persisted to RADOS or the journal.
qa/suites/fs/workload/tasks/5-dmclock/yes.yaml enables QoS with defaults in fs workload runs. No other test references the feature.
doc/cephfs/mds-qos.rst promises per-subvolume buckets from /volumes/<group>/<subvolume>, cost 1 for reads and 3 for mutations, reservation/weight/limit meanings, and non-persistent overrides.

rust_implications.implication: No client, mon, mgr or OSD protocol carries QoS information. The Rust MDS is free to redesign QoS completely. Only the operator-facing names (mds_dmclock_* options, dump qos / qos set|get|rm) and doc/cephfs/mds-qos.rst set expectations, and nothing in mgr/cephadm consumes them.

Unmodified clients only provide session metadata 'root' (client-asserted, validated against caps at open). A per-subvolume SLA engine should classify by the authoritative subvolume of the request's target inode or shard, rather than by the session root. This covers root-mounted clients such as Ganesha with cmount_path=/, the mgr and cephfs-mirror. Session-root classification can remain a fallback.

rust_implications.topic: Throttle by delay, not by error
rust_implications.implication: Clients cannot handle EAGAIN or back-pressure replies for metadata ops. Over-limit requests must be held, as with C++ AtLimit::Wait. The kclient mount GETATTR times out after 60 s and libcephfs mount requests after 300 s, so the session-bootstrap path should be exempt or prioritized.

C++ queues are unbounded once the messenger throttle is released. The Rust design should bound per-session and per-subvolume queues and push back at the transport level (stop reading the connection) instead of buffering without limit.

Holding requests while caps, cap releases, leases and session messages from the same connection are processed changes per-connection processing order. Either preserve per-session FIFO across all message classes that can interact, or prove commutation for each pair. Keep per-session request FIFO in all cases.

rust_implications.topic: Integrate QoS into the shard scheduler
rust_implications.implication: In C++ the QoS threads hand off one request at a time under a global lock while holding the queue mutex. In the proposed architecture, admission and rate limits belong in each subvolume shard's queue in the Concurrent Execution Scheduler, with timer-driven wakeups instead of a polling thread, and with no global lock in the admission path.

C++ dmClock has can_handle=true, so reservation and weight are nearly meaningless. For real reservations and weights, the Rust scheduler needs a capacity signal (worker slots, journal bandwidth, per-shard in-flight budget) and should charge cost for actual work (journal bytes, lock waits, cross-shard 2PC), not only the op code.

C++ overrides are memory-only, per rank, and lost on failover or when the last session closes. A per-subvolume SLA needs durable per-subvolume QoS config stored with the subvolume shard and replayed with it, and a policy for clients that talk to several ranks or shards (C++ charges each rank independently; forwarded requests are charged twice).

rust_implications.topic: Count queue time in op tracking
rust_implications.implication: In C++, queued requests are invisible to op dumps until dispatch, but their age starts at receive time, so slow-request health can fire because of QoS. Expose queued requests and QoS wait explicitly, and decide whether QoS-induced waits count as slow requests.
C++ re-charges message-level retries (C_MDS_RetryMessage) and requests forwarded across ranks. Charge once per client request id per shard.

Do not tie QoS state lifetime to session counts with assertions (crash on evicting a throttled client). Do not drain by sleeping while holding control threads. Use a single lock order. Keep config hot-reload free of asserts on float equality.
dmClock tags use CLOCK_REALTIME, so wall-clock steps stall or release queues. Use a monotonic clock for all QoS tags.
